choices.text: Nothing - the rock crumbles on its own

questions.feedback: If you picked nothing, that is the trap: Rocks crumble on their own, with nothing doing the wearing. Reteach point: Rocks do not crumble on their own: moving water and wind do the wearing, loosening and carrying the bits away.
questions.misconception: Rocks crumble on their own, with nothing doing the wearing.
questions.prompt: What wears rock away in erosion?

questions.answer: Erosion is the wearing away of rock by moving water and wind, which loosen bits of rock and carry them away.
questions.feedback: A strong answer names both halves: a mover (moving water or wind) doing the wearing, and the bits being carried away. An answer with no mover is missing the main idea.
questions.prompt: In one sentence, explain what erosion is.

choices.text: It climbs back up the cliff
It stays floating in one spot forever
The current carries it away along the coast

questions.feedback: Once a bit is loose, moving water takes over: the current carries it away. That carrying away is why the cliff loses rock for good.
questions.prompt: A loose bit has just broken off the cliff. What most likely happens to it next?

questions.answer: Because there is no mover doing the wearing: without moving water or wind, nothing batters, loosens or carries the rock, so the cliff stays almost the same.
questions.feedback: The missing ingredient is movement: erosion needs moving water or wind. Still air and a flat sea do almost no wearing at all.
questions.prompt: Why does a cliff change very little on a calm day with no waves and no wind?
